text:
Alex: Running a 36h streaming-chat + toolloop soak on dedicated pool A, observed steady RSS growth ~12MB/hr despite KV page evictions triggering. Not a simple leak in VM mappings, looks like allocator fragmentation or stale refs.
Maya: ugh. Which workload? long-toolloop or user chats with long toolchains?
Alex: toolloop heavy — many short messages but very long aggregate prefix (avg context ~120k tokens). Repro steps: `./run_soak --scenario=toolloop --concurrency=50 --long-context=120000`
Jordan: Can you paste pprof heap top and a quick `pprof -alloc_objects -top` snapshot?
Alex: quick snippet from 2026-03-15 04:12 UTC heap top: ```
(pprof) top10
Showing nodes accounting for 87.4MB, 72.6% of 120.4MB total
Dropped 120 nodes (cum <= 0.60MB)
      flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   node
    32.1MB 26.7% 26.7%     32.1MB 26.7%  runtime.mallocgc
    20.5MB 17.0% 43.7%     25.4MB 21.1%  github.com/redwood/kv.(*page).holdRefs
    12.8MB 10.6% 54.3%     18.7MB 15.5%  github.com/redwood/serving/cache.(*slab).allocHeader
```
Alex: note `page.holdRefs` and `slab.allocHeader` both show up consistently.
Priya: I ran a smaller repro with `--trace-kv` enabled, logs show frequent `evict -> free` but many `header reclaim skipped: refcount!=0`. Possible stale refcounts.
Jordan: Could be double-path retention: streaming path increments ref, background eviction path expects decrement but race. Any recent kernel selection or batching changes?
Maya: We shipped batching heuristics refactor last week. It touches KV hot-path for `prefetch` -> may affect ref lifetimes.
Sam: repro: toggling `KV_PREFETCH=false` in config reduced growth rate by ~70% in 6h run. So prefetch seems implicated.
Alex: Good catch. But why would prefetching leave refs held? Hypothesis: prefetch attaches a short-living reader that isn't closed when the request falls through to fallback variant (model swap).
Priya: I dumped goroutine stacks at 2h intervals, found a lot of goroutines stuck in `kv/page.go:Hold()` with stuck stack waiting on `slab.mu` during heavy compaction. They eventually unblock but leave headers pinned.
Jordan: Could be ordering: `Hold()` increments ref before acquiring slab-level lock, `Evict()` expects to get same lock to clear refs — race window. If prefetch creates a temporary hold and returns without Release on error path, header remains.
Alex: Attached a flamegraph link (internal): https://grafana/redwood/fg/1955001234 - high tail on `page.hold` and `allocHeader`
Maya: What about forcing compaction on evict? We added a config `KV_COMPACT_ON_EVICT` but default was off. Any experiments?
Sam: I ran with `KV_COMPACT_ON_EVICT=true` for 12h, growth plateaued after compaction but still spiky. So compaction helps but doesn't fully fix root cause.
Priya: Here's a small repro I pushed to `eng-runtime/repro/toolloop-kv-leak`: `./repro --loops=1000 --prefetch` it will allocate then yield an error path often. Logs show `Hold()` call without matching `Release()` about ~0.7% of times.
Jordan: 0.7% could explain slow steady growth across many sessions. Let's add asserts in dev build to track unmatched holds: increment metric `kv.holds_unmatched`->should be 0.
Alex: I can run a dev build on canary for 6h with asserts and metrics. Will need a rollback plan if noisy.
Maya: Also enable jemalloc background defrag on canary to reduce visible RSS while we fix. `MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,metadata_thp:false` (example).
Sam: CI-Bot: test run for `kv` package on PR #7281 shows `kv.hold` leak detector flagged 3 failures in unit tests.
CI-Bot: PR #7281 — kv: add hold/release assertions — CI failed: unit:kv (3 fails), e2e:serving (flaky). See https://ci.redwood/7281
Priya: Unit failures are expected because tests didn't call Release in error paths; I'll fix tests and add coverage for prefetch error branches.
Jordan: Long-term: we should audit all code paths that call `page.Hold()` and ensure `defer page.Release()` pattern or use RAII-like wrapper `withHold(page, func(){...})`.
Alex: For immediate mitigation: 1) flip off `KV_PREFETCH` on Canaries 2) enable `KV_COMPACT_ON_EVICT` 3) push dev build with unmatched-hold metric and alerts > 10/min.
Maya: Agree. Also schedule a run with `--long-context=200k` to stress compaction boundaries.
Sam: I'll prepare the rollout playbook: quick toggle env var, monitor `kv.holds_unmatched` and `rss_growth_rate`, rollback if user-facing latency regresses >10%.
Priya: After enabling dev build locally, I reproded and saw `kv.holds_unmatched` spike to 42 over 3h. The stack traces point to `prefetch.go:prefetchWorker` error return path. Fix is small: ensure `defer h.Release()` at top of function.
Alex: Great. Can you open a PR and tag me? If it's that small we can hotfix to canary and then to prod.
Priya: PR #7290 opened: `kv: ensure Release on prefetch error paths` — includes unit test that fails without fix.
CI-Bot: PR #7290 — CI passed: unit:kv ✅ e2e:serving ✅.
Jordan: Once deployed to canary, run 24h soak with prior config: prefetch disabled on baseline, then enable prefetch w/ fix. Compare RSS slope.
Maya: Also add an autosample to logs for `evict` events so we can correlate `evict` -> `hold` sequences during production incidents.
Alex: I pushed the canary with fix at 2026-03-15 18:00 UTC. After 16h, growth rate dropped to noise (1.2MB/hr) vs 12MB/hr previously. Looks like root cause fixed.
Sam: Nice. Follow-up: schedule a postmortem doc summarizing timeline, root cause, fix, and a checklist to avoid missing Release in future.
Priya: I'll draft the postmortem and add lessons: prefer RAII helper, add unmatched-hold metric, add unit tests for error paths.
Alex: Thanks everyone :tada:
Maya: Amazing work.
CI-Bot: Deployed canary -> prod rollout succeeded at 2026-03-16 10:12 UTC.
